about: CMB on Alarm and MB-by-MB on Alarm, Hailfinder, and the 45 x 45 chessboard against global PC read at the target, on their papers' settings; a row judges its first solution, and the release summary's CMB and MB-by-MB entries are built from these rows
build: CMB: Andrey pre-release build of 13 November 2026 (the 0.18.0 release branch as merged with LOAD's skeleton step); the release branch of 14 November 2026, with exact upper-tail p-values, gave the same answers and test counts at every target of the 3 datasets rerun | MB-by-MB: Andrey pre-release build of 14 November 2026 (the 0.18.0 release branch with MB-by-MB's independence rule)
hardware: CMB: AMD EPYC 7713 64-Core Processor, 1 core per fit, 1 BLAS thread; CMB, Andrey's PC, and bnlearn ran in the same run, one fit after the other, on shared nodes, so the times are indicative | MB-by-MB: AMD EPYC 7713 64-Core Processor, 1 core per fit, 1 BLAS thread; MB-by-MB, CMB, and the two PCs ran in separate runs on shared nodes, so the times are indicative
verdict_rule: CMB: no reference implementation exists, so each row sets Andrey's means beside the paper's (Table 1) and judges CMB against two global PCs read at the target, Andrey's pc with the same test and level and bnlearn 5.2.1 pc.stable with mi-adf: the mean over paired datasets of CMB's total minus the other's with its 95% percentile-bootstrap interval, better or worse when the interval lies wholly on that side of 0 over at least 10 datasets, on seeds 0-19, and a cell worse there counts only when it is worse again on seeds 20-39. The floor: per dataset, the total minus the empty answer's; a row passes when its interval lies wholly below 0 | MB-by-MB: no reference implementation exists, so each row sets Andrey's means beside the paper's (Tables 1-3) and judges MB-by-MB against two global PCs read at the target, Andrey's pc and bnlearn 5.2.1 pc.stable with mi-adf, both with the same test and level and at most 5 conditioning variables, the paper's cap, and against Andrey's CMB at the same level where it ran: the mean over paired datasets of MB-by-MB's shd minus the other's with its 95% percentile-bootstrap interval, better or worse when the interval lies wholly on that side of 0 over at least 10 datasets, on the first seeds, and a cell worse there counts only when it is worse again on the fresh seeds. A comparison dominates a cell when it is more accurate and takes fewer tests per answer; the tests over every target are context. The floor: per dataset, the shd minus the empty answer's; a row passes when its interval lies wholly below 0
error_metric: CMB: total: per target, the edges at the target missing or extra against the true CPDAG plus those whose direction differs from it, an edge the CPDAG directs and the answer leaves undirected included (reversed); a dataset's value is the mean over its targets. lenient leaves out the undirected ones. The floor uses the total against the empty answer's, the target's degree | MB-by-MB: shd: per target, the edges at the target against the true DAG, an edge the answer leaves undirected (undirected), a true edge it misses (miss), an edge the DAG lacks (extra), and a directed edge whose direction differs (reverse), shd their sum; a dataset's value is the mean over its targets. The floor uses the shd against the empty answer's, the target's degree. Cost per answer, what answering one target costs: MB-by-MB's and CMB's tests at that target, a global PC's whole fit; cost over every target: their sum over the targets, the one fit
fit_protocol: CMB: each fit in a fresh process on one core with one BLAS thread, CMB once per target and each PC once per dataset, read at every target; no warm-up, a cap of 1,800 s per fit, past which a fit is a timeout and never scored; no fit failed or timed out. G-square tests at alpha 0.02 with no limit on the conditioning set, CMB with HITON-MB, its default blanket learner | MB-by-MB: each run fits a range of one cell's datasets in one process, one core and one BLAS thread, a cell's datasets in one run or in several over seed ranges (CMB at Hailfinder's 500 and 1,000 rows ran in several runs per cell); MB-by-MB and CMB once per target and each PC once per dataset, read at every target; no warm-up, a cap of 1,800 s per fit, 3,600 s on the chessboard, past which a fit is a timeout and never scored; no fit failed or timed out. G-square tests at the cell's level, MB-by-MB with its defaults, IAMB's forward phase for the blankets and at most 5 conditioning variables in the local structures; CMB with HITON-MB, its default
seeds_note: CMB: every cell holds 20 datasets, seeds 0-19, and 20 fresh datasets, seeds 20-39 | MB-by-MB: Alarm and Hailfinder cells hold 20 datasets, seeds 0-19, and 20 fresh datasets, seeds 20-39; chessboard cells hold 10 datasets, seeds 0-9, and 10 fresh datasets, seeds 10-19, with fresh PC fits at 500 and 1,000 rows
cells_note: CMB: net:alarm:1000: forward samples of the Alarm network's own tables, the columns in an order drawn from the seed; every answer is scored at each target against the CPDAG | MB-by-MB: net:<network>:<rows>: forward samples of Alarm's or Hailfinder's own tables, every node a target, or of the 45 x 45 chessboard, its tables drawn from the seed and its 10 fixed squares the targets, the columns in an order drawn from the seed; every answer is scored at each target against the true DAG
